title: Derivative of the Gaussian quantile
statement: Let $\Phi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function, define $Q(\alpha)=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R: \alpha\leq\Phi(t)\}$, and set $I(\alpha)=\varphi(Q(\alpha))$, where $\varphi$ is the standard Gaussian density. For $a\in(0,1)$, $Q$ is differentiable at $a$ with derivative $1/I(a)$.
replaced: Let $\Phi$ and $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian distribution function and density, and put $Q=\Phi^{-1}$ and $I(p)=\varphi(Q(p))$ for $0<p<1$. For every $a\in(0,1)$, $Q'(a)=1/I(a)$.
